metadata.description: Single-plugin marketplace exposing the cc-enforcer discipline plugin.

plugins.name: cc-enforcer
plugins.description: Rules your coding agent physically cannot ignore. A Claude Code plugin (and LLM-agnostic rule pack) that stops reactive patching, guessed citations, surface-level fixes and premature "done" claims by intercepting the agent's own tool calls rather than asking it nicely. PreToolUse denies an edit before it lands — editing a file you never opened this session, a suppression marker with no adjacent why-comment, a hardcoded secret or user-home path, the fourth small patch to one file, a dangerous shell flag. A nine-layer Stop gate then refuses to let a completion claim end the turn without evidence, a convergence self-quiz, a fidelity check against the user's ORIGINAL request, and a one-line TL;DR. Twelve rules, eight backed by a hook; "Imperial Edict" regexes you define per project; a repo-wide sync gate; CI drift gates that derive every documented number from the code so the documentation cannot rot. Zero dependencies, stdlib only, Linux + Windows CI, and every guard fails OPEN — a bug in the discipline can never brick your agent. v0.37.0 fixes the boundary every single hook invocation passes through. Each entry point read its payload with `sys.stdin.read()`, which decodes with the HOST codepage under the `surrogateescape` error handler — so on any machine whose codepage is not UTF-8 (the default on Windows) the JSON arrived silently rewritten, and every guard scanned a string the agent never wrote. No exception, no stderr, no failing test. Measured on cp936, an em-dash arrived as two characters instead of one, enough to push an inline note past the rule-09 rationale floor and turn a DENY into an ALLOW: the guard was defeated by punctuation. The Stop gate lost far more. `大白话`, `同步核对`, `我觉得` and the done-claim patterns themselves are Chinese, so all of them decoded to mojibake and the CJK half of nine layers matched nothing in production — `_has_done_claim` gates all nine layers and its pattern set is bilingual, so a reply that announced completion only in Chinese matched nothing and skipped the entire stack — measured, a bare completion claim carrying no evidence at all came back allowed with not one layer having fired. Stated precisely rather than loosely, because the looser version would be exactly the overstatement this plugin exists to block: a reply that also said "done" or "fixed" in ASCII still reached layer (a). What it could not do was fail on a Chinese hedge, a Chinese TL;DR marker, or a Chinese sync-check line — those markers were not there to be found. This is the same class the v0.25 `tomlio` hardening closed one boundary over (a wrong decode silently disabling enforcement rather than reporting anything), swept twelve releases late to the boundary that carries every payload. Fixed at the mechanism in a new shared module, `lib/hookio.py`: read stdin's binary buffer, decode UTF-8 strictly per RFC 8259, and let a genuinely malformed payload raise into the existing fail-open handler — loud and diagnosable instead of quietly mangled. Why it survived 691 tests: `tests/_helpers.py` serialised with `json.dumps`, whose `ensure_ascii=True` default escaped every non-ASCII character to a `\uXXXX` sequence before the bytes existed, so the wire was pure ASCII and the decode step had nothing to get wrong — the fixtures could not reach the region the defect lives in, the same shape as the v0.35 `editscale` finding where every fixture happened to be one line long. The harness now puts raw UTF-8 on the wire and a test pins that it does, because restoring the default would re-hide the whole class while leaving everything else green. The end-to-end cases force `PYTHONIOENCODING=cp936:surrogateescape` so a defect that only appears on a non-UTF-8 host still fails on the UTF-8 CI runner, and a vacuity guard fails loudly if that reproduction ever stops biting, so a future Python cannot turn the file green for the wrong reason. Five cases were verified RED against the pre-fix tree; the rest are labelled as controls. 691 -> 712 tests. Prior — v0.36.0 adds a demo you can run yourself: the same task, twice, against identical starting files, with the hooks as the only variable. `charge()` raises KeyError when the payment gateway declines — loud, immediate, pointing straight at the line that caused it. WITHOUT the plugin all five reactive edits land: the crash is swallowed into a `None`, the suite turns red, and a sign-off claiming it is green ends the turn with nothing checking the claim. WITH the plugin three of the five are refused — the `try/except: pass`, the fourth small patch to the same file, and the evidence-free completion claim — and the run is pushed into one systematic rewrite that names the root cause (the gateway has two response shapes and the old body knew only one). The subject is the LAGGING error: patching a loud failure does not remove it, it makes it quiet. A stack trace becomes a ledger holding rows the gateway never accepted, and nothing reports it until someone reconciles a statement weeks later. Both transcripts render to terminal SVGs embedded in both READMEs, replacing the hand-drawn 'before' mock-ups they used to carry. Every cc-enforcer verdict in the images is verbatim hook stdout, every test and probe result is captured from a real run, and the agent's five moves are scripted — stated plainly, because a demo that overstated itself would be the exact defect this plugin exists to catch. tests/test_demo.py re-runs the demo and compares against the committed images byte for byte, so a change to any hook's wording fails CI instead of leaving a stale picture on the front page; and because that equality check alone would be satisfied by a demo that had stopped denying anything, it also asserts each of the three verdicts by content and asserts the unguarded run still ends in a silent failure. 682 -> 690 tests, then 691 in v0.36.1, which fixed the demo images: they were rendered on Windows, so the deny banner carried a backslash-joined path that Linux reproduces with a forward slash, and a byte-for-byte pinned artefact may not contain a platform-dependent string. Fixed at the mechanism and asserted by its own test. Full release history: CHANGELOG.md.
